title: Few picnics, many nightclubs, and advertising trucks
summary: Trotter mostly played nightclubs around New Orleans and did advertising truck jobs with short bands.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: Lucha, that was Anderson's job. June the 6th, must have been a picnic. Mm-hmm. Did you play many picnics in the 30s? Not too many. Not too many. Not too many. I played too many picnics. Mostly my playing was, you know, like these little gigs around these little nightclubs. I played plenty of nightclubs. I played in practically every place here in New Orleans. You know, the Rhythm Club, New Orleans Country Club. Well, I played there with Celestine, but I'm just saying practically all these little nightclubs I played in. Cali, Enter, the Opera House and all those places. I played in all of those. That's where my work was mostly done around there then, you know. Then up here they had this Seventh and Howard Grand Terrace, I told you, and the Black Gold and all those places. But I didn't play too many picnics. Now, we used to advertise on trucks then. I did a lot of that. Advertising, but I didn't do no parading, but advertising on the trucks.
Did they have big bands on the trucks or short bands? Short bands. About hundred and a pieces.
About five or six pieces like that. You ever buck? Yeah, they probably had.
